MAC STORAGE GUIDE

How to clear space on Mac safely

Follow this safe 3-step workflow to reclaim storage. Review large files, app leftovers, duplicate files, and system data caches without risky terminal commands.

01
Check Mac storage breakdown

Open System Settings > General > Storage to see what is using disk space before deleting anything.

02
Scan with on-device Mac cleaner

Use Smart Cleaner AI to find large files, duplicate files, old downloads, unused apps, and clearable caches.

03
Review side-by-side & clean to Trash

Inspect file locations and sizes, keep what you need, and send unwanted clutter to Trash with a recovery option until Trash is emptied.

STORAGE BREAKDOWN

What Smart Cleaner AI Finds on Your Mac

All scans run 100% on-device. We clearly categorize which items are generally safe to remove and which need closer review.

ITEM CATEGORY	RISK PROFILE	HOW SMART CLEANER AI HANDLES IT
App & User Caches	
Generally Recreated as Needed	Outdated web caches, media thumbnails, and temporary application files. Apps automatically regenerate these caches as needed.
System & Diagnostic Logs	
Usually Safe to Clear	Historical crash logs, install records, and diagnostic reports that can be safely cleared to reclaim disk space.
Orphaned App Leftovers	
Safe After Review	Detects hidden Application Support folders, preference plists, and crash helpers left behind by previously deleted apps.
Duplicate Files & Archives	
Review Recommended	Identical files and installers saved in different folders. Shows byte-level matches side-by-side so you choose which version to keep.
Large & Forgotten Files (>100MB)	
Review Recommended	Old .dmg installers, heavy zip archives, and forgotten exports sorted by last-opened date to help you declutter manually.
Developer Caches (Xcode DerivedData)	
Regenerates on Next Build	Removing Xcode DerivedData and build artifacts safely frees up substantial space, though projects will take longer to index and compile on their next build.
